record.paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
record.original_question: Does there exist a Banach space X such that its bidual X** has the Daugavet property, meaning that every finite-rank operator T from X** to X** satisfies ||Id + T|| = 1 + ||T||?

evidence.quote: A Banach space X has the Daugavet property if every finite rank operator T : X → X satisfies kId + Tk = 1 + kTk.
Problem 2.1. Do there exist bidual Banach spaces with the Daugavet property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach space $X$ is said to have the Daugavet property if every bounded finite-rank linear operator $T : X \to X$ satisfies the norm equality
$$\|\mathrm{Id} + T\| = 1 + \|T\|,$$
where $\mathrm{Id}$ denotes the identity operator on $X$.

For a Banach space $X$, let $X^{**}$ denote its bidual, i.e., the topological dual of $X^*$, regarded as a Banach space with its canonical norm.

Question: Does there exist a Banach space $X$ such that the bidual $X^{**}$ has the Daugavet property?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface active research on the Daugavet property and its bidual characterizations (e.g., L-orthogonality criteria, polynomial Daugavet property), but none of the recent sources explicitly announce a resolution of the question of whether a bidual Banach space can carry the Daugavet property. The status appears to remain unsettled based on the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Banach spaces with the Daugavet property (Kadets–Martín–Rueda Zoca–Werner)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive monograph on the Daugavet property including open questions sections; no announced resolution of the bidual existence question.
status_evidence.claim: The question is treated within the ongoing research literature on the Daugavet property without an announced resolution.

status_evidence.title: L-orthogonality, octahedrality and Daugavet property in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes the Daugavet property via weak-star density of L-orthogonal vectors in the bidual.
status_evidence.claim: Bidual characterizations of the Daugavet property are an active topic, but do not directly resolve whether a bidual space can have the Daugavet property.
